objective_for_doctor:
Age: 8
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have right side of the chest pain, left side of the chest pain, and upper chest pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have chest pain on both sides—right side, left side, and also upper chest pain. It feels like a knife-stab, very violent pain (about 8/10), and it started really fast. I also feel short of breath, especially when I move, and it hurts more when I breathe in.

I’m sorry you’re going through that. One question at a time:

**1) When the pain started, did it happen suddenly at rest (seconds to minutes), and have you had any fainting, severe sweating, or feeling like you might pass out?**
Yes, it started really suddenly—within seconds to minutes—while I was just at rest. I haven’t fainted, and I don’t feel like I’m going to pass out, and I don’t have severe sweating.
**2) Does the pain get worse with deep breathing or coughing (pleuritic pain), and do you notice any leg swelling or pain in one leg?**
Yes, it gets worse with deep breathing. I don’t know about coughing— I can’t say for sure—but the breathing-in makes it worse. I don’t have leg swelling or pain in one leg.
**3) Do you have any fever, cough, or recent flu-like illness (like sore throat, runny nose, body aches)?**
No fever. I don’t have a cough or recent flu-like illness—no sore throat, runny nose, or body aches.
**4) Have you had any recent long travel, surgery, immobilization, or are you on estrogen-containing birth control or hormone therapy?**
No recent long travel, and I haven’t had surgery or been immobilized. I’m not on any hormone medicine.
**5) Do you have any history of lung disease (asthma/COPD), heart rhythm problems, or prior blood clots?**
I don’t have asthma or COPD, and no heart rhythm problems that I know of. But I’ve had a spontaneous pneumothorax before. I don’t know of any blood clots.
**6) With this episode, do you feel any sudden worsening of shortness of breath compared with normal, and do you notice one-sided chest tightness or “air hunger”?**
Yes, my breathing feels much worse suddenly compared to normal. It feels tight and like I can’t get enough air—air hunger. It’s on both sides though, not just one side.
**7) When you take a breath, is it mainly painful (sharp) or is it also difficult to move air (wheezing/whistling)? Any audible wheeze?**
It’s mainly painful and sharp when I breathe in. I don’t hear any wheezing or whistling, and it’s not like I’m making an audible sound.
**8) Do you have any recent trauma to the chest (fall, heavy lifting, coughing hard), or pain that’s reproducible when you press on your chest wall?**
No recent trauma like a fall or heavy lifting. I also can’t say it’s reproducible when pressing on my chest wall—it feels more like the breathing makes it worse.
**9) Are you having any palpitations (feeling your heart racing/irregular), or have you measured a fast heart rate?**
No palpitations that I notice, and I haven’t measured my heart rate.

**10) Do you have any risk factors for heart disease (high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, high cholesterol, strong family history of early heart attack), or is the pain clearly “knife-stab” rather than pressure/heaviness?**
I don’t have those heart disease risk factors that I know of, and it’s more like a knife-stab/violent sharp pain, not pressure or heaviness.
**11) Any leg symptoms at all—new one-sided calf pain, redness, or swelling—or coughing up blood?**
No leg symptoms like one-sided calf pain, redness, or swelling. And I’m not coughing up blood.
**12) Do you have any upper respiratory symptoms at all right now (sore throat, hoarseness, trouble swallowing), or any swelling/itching/rash?**
No upper respiratory symptoms like sore throat or hoarseness, and no trouble swallowing. I also don’t have swelling, itching, or a rash.
**13) Any history of anxiety/panic attacks, or does the pain come with tingling, feeling of doom, or hyperventilation?**
No history of anxiety or panic attacks. I’m just in a lot of pain and short of breath from it. I don’t have tingling or a feeling of doom.
**14) On a scale of 0–10, how bad is the shortness of breath, and can you speak full sentences without stopping to breathe?**
My shortness of breath is significant—about 8/10 with the pain. I can’t really speak full sentences without stopping to breathe.
